set.title: Fact fluency & order of operations · Unit Test

questions.question: What is 56 ÷ 8?
questions.explain: Think of the matching multiplication fact: 8 × 7 = 56, so 56 ÷ 8 = 7. A common trap is mixing up the two partners in the fact family and answering 8 (that is 56 ÷ 7).

questions.question: Evaluate: 7 + 4 × 5
questions.explain: Multiply before you add: 4 × 5 = 20, then 7 + 20 = 27. The most common mistake is working left to right (7 + 4 = 11, then 11 × 5 = 55).

questions.question: Evaluate: (8 + 4) × 3
questions.explain: Brackets come first: 8 + 4 = 12, then 12 × 3 = 36. Students who ignore the brackets multiply first and get 8 + 12 = 20.

questions.question: A case of juice boxes holds 26 boxes. The Grade 6 class brings 4 full cases to sports day. Using double-double, how many juice boxes is that in total?
questions.explain: Double-double for × 4: double 26 to get 52, then double 52 to get 104. The usual slip is stopping after one double (52) or forgetting the 6 and only doing 4 × 20 = 80.

questions.question: Priya has 72 hockey cards. She puts them into piles of 8 cards each. How many piles does she make?
questions.explain: Divide: 72 ÷ 8 = 9, because 8 × 9 = 72. Watch for two traps — subtracting instead of dividing (72 − 8 = 64), or grabbing the wrong partner fact and saying 8.

questions.question: Amara pays with a $20 bill for 3 packs of pencils that cost $4 each. Which expression shows the change she gets back?
questions.explain: Find the cost first (3 × 4 = 12), then subtract it from 20, which the expression 20 − 3 × 4 does automatically because multiplication happens before subtraction. Adding brackets as in (20 − 3) × 4 changes the meaning and subtracts the number of packs instead of their cost.

questions.question: Evaluate: 36 ÷ (2 + 4) × 3
questions.explain: Brackets first: 2 + 4 = 6. Then division and multiplication are done left to right: 36 ÷ 6 = 6, and 6 × 3 = 18. The big trap is thinking multiplication always beats division and doing 6 × 3 = 18 first, which gives 36 ÷ 18 = 2.

questions.question: Mateo saves $8 every week for 5 weeks. Then he buys 2 comic books that cost $9 each. Written as one expression, 8 × 5 − 2 × 9, how much money does he have left?
questions.explain: Do both multiplications first: 8 × 5 = 40 saved and 2 × 9 = 18 spent, so 40 − 18 = $22. Common traps are paying for only one comic book ($31) or subtracting the number of books instead of their cost ($38).
